findings.summary: Page 1 ends with the last-occurrence and upper-bound templates, two patterns that are not introduced until section 3 on pages 2-3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 final two code blocks: `"// lastOccurrence: same loop", "if (arr[mid] == target) {", "  ans = mid;     // potential", "  low = mid + 1; // right half"` (note: "Move RIGHT when target is found") and `"int low = 0, high = n;" ... "return low; // first arr[i] > t"` (note: "gotcha: loop is while (low < high)"), while the heading "3. First & Last Occurrence + Bounds" appears on page 2 and "5. Upper Bound" on page 3.
findings.fix: Move both code blocks to page 3: the lastOccurrence snippet directly under the "2. Last Occurrence (Upper Bound - 1)" sidebox, and the upperBound snippet directly under the "5. Upper Bound" sidebox. End page 1 with the Move Left vs Right table.

findings.summary: The infinite-array range-doubling code is the first block of page 2, sitting inside the classic-template section three pages before infinite arrays are introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 2 block 1: `"int low = 0, high = 1;", "while (arr[high] < target) {", "  low = high;   // find range", "  high = high * 2;", "}", "return bs(arr, low, high, target);"` — but "Array size is ==unknown== (infinite)" first appears at the end of page 5 and the worked example on page 6.
findings.fix: Move this code block to page 6, immediately after the "Array size is unknown (infinite)" bullets and before the "Example arr = [1,3,5,7,9,...], target = 14" paragraph, which currently walks through an expansion loop the reader has never seen.

findings.summary: The code block presented under the "5. Upper Bound" sidebox actually computes the lower bound, not the upper bound.
findings.evidence: Sidebox "5. Upper Bound" states "Goal: first index where `arr[i] > target`" and "If all elements <= target, return **n**", but the code immediately under it reads "if (arr[mid] >= target)" / "high = mid;" / "else low = mid + 1;" / "return low; // first arr[i] >= t" — the comment itself states the lower-bound definition.
findings.fix: Change the comparison to `if (arr[mid] > target) high = mid;` and the comment to `// first arr[i] > t`, matching the correct upper-bound template already shown on page 1 ("return low; // first arr[i] > t").

findings.summary: The two bound goal boxes on page 3 are each followed by the wrong template: first-occurrence code under Lower Bound, lower-bound code under Upper Bound.
findings.evidence: "4. Lower Bound" ("Goal: first index where `arr[i] >= target`") is followed by `"if (arr[mid] == target) {", "ans = mid;     // potential", "high = mid - 1; // left half"` (note "Move LEFT when target is found"); "5. Upper Bound" ("Goal: first index where `arr[i] > target`") is followed by `"if (arr[mid] >= target)", "high = mid;", "return low; // first arr[i] >= t"`.
findings.fix: Re-pair the blocks: put the firstOccurrence template on page 2 under the "1. First Occurrence (Lower Bound)" sidebox, keep the `arr[mid] >= target` template under "4. Lower Bound", and place the `arr[mid] > target` template (currently on page 1) under "5. Upper Bound".

findings.summary: The second array diagram's "Step 2 / Step 3" continues searching for 16 after Step 1 already returned it, and its pointer state is unreachable from Step 1.
findings.evidence: Step 1 caption: "low=0, mid=4, high=8, arr[mid] == 16 -> found at index 4". Step 2 diagram then sets pointers low=0, mid=2, high=5 with caption "Step 2: mid=2, arr[mid] = 8 < 16 -> search RIGHT; Step 3: mid lands on 16, found" — but a hit at mid=4 terminates the search, and no branch from low=0/high=8 produces high=5.
findings.fix: Make the two diagrams one coherent run: either drop the Step 2/3 diagram, or change Step 1's target so it misses (e.g. target = 8: arr[4]=16 > 8 -> high = 3) and redraw Step 2 with the pointers that actually follow.

findings.summary: In the fundamentals flowchart, the "repeat" edge label is rendered twice on top of itself and collides with the bottom border of the "return mid (found)" oval.
findings.evidence: Directly beneath the green "return mid (found)" oval the word "repeat" appears as two superimposed copies ("repeat" over "repeat"), striking through the oval's lower stroke, instead of one legible label on the loop-back edge.
findings.fix: Render the loop-back edge label once and offset it clear of the oval — move the "repeat" label onto the vertical connector below the oval (or to the right of the edge) with enough padding that it does not intersect the node border.

findings.summary: The code shown under the "4. Lower Bound" sidebox is the first-occurrence routine, which returns -1 on a miss instead of the n the sidebox promises.
findings.evidence: Sidebox "4. Lower Bound" says "Goal: first index where `arr[i] >= target`" and "If all elements < target, return **n**", but the code under it is "int ans = -1; ... if (arr[mid] == target) { ans = mid; high = mid - 1; } ... return ans;" with note "Move LEFT when target is found" — it only ever records exact matches.
findings.fix: Pair the Lower Bound sidebox with the `low = 0, high = n; while (low < high) { if (arr[mid] >= target) high = mid; else low = mid + 1; } return low;` template, and move the ans/-1 snippet back under the First Occurrence heading on page 2.

findings.summary: Every hour count in the Koko Eating Bananas dry-run table is arithmetically wrong for piles = [3,6,7,11].
findings.evidence: Table rows: "1,1,11,6,Yes (8 hours)"; "2,1,5,3,No (9 hours)"; "3,4,5,4,Yes (7 hours)" with note "piles = [3,6,7,11], H = 8". Actual sums of ceil(p/speed): speed 6 -> 1+1+2+2 = 6 hours; speed 3 -> 1+2+3+4 = 10 hours; speed 4 -> 1+2+2+3 = 8 hours.
findings.fix: Replace the isPossible column values with "Yes (6 hours)", "No (10 hours)", "Yes (8 hours)"; the Yes/No verdicts and final answer = 4 stay unchanged (8 <= H = 8).

findings.summary: Page 4 dry-runs the rotated-array target search before the sorted-half search code, which only appears on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with the table row `["1","0","6","3","7","left [4..7] sorted, 2 not inside -> go **RIGHT**"]`, while the code `"if (arr[low] <= arr[mid]) {", "  // left half sorted", ...` is block 3 of page 5.
findings.fix: Move the rotated-array search code block from page 5 to page 4, directly after the "Key Idea" callout and before the dry-run table.

findings.summary: Page 5 opens with duplicate handling for the rotated-array search before the no-duplicates search algorithm it modifies appears later on the same page.
findings.evidence: Page 5 block 1: "arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high] -> can't tell which half is sorted" and "Otherwise apply the normal sorted-half check", but the sorted-half code (`"if (arr[low] <= arr[mid]) {", "  // left half sorted"`, note "no duplicates; return false after loop") is block 3.
findings.fix: Once the search code moves to page 4, start page 5 with the "5. Find Minimum Element" sidebox, then the duplicates bullets and the O(n) note, so the base algorithm always precedes its variant.

findings.summary: The Search Insert Position section is taught on page 6 but its template is stranded as the first block of page 7, after the reader has already been shown the results table.
findings.evidence: Page 6: "Classic loop; on a miss, return low" and the table rows `["5","2","exists"],["2","1","insert at index 1"]`; page 7 block 1: `"while (low <= high) {" ... "return low; // insertion position"` (note "on miss, low is the insert slot").
findings.fix: Move the searchInsert code block to page 6, between the "Target exists -> return its index" bullets and the nums = [1,3,5,6] results table.

findings.summary: The comparison bound is understated: binary search needs floor(log2 n) + 1 comparisons in the worst case, not at most log2(n).
findings.evidence: "Cost: **at most log₂(n)** comparisons." For this page's own 9-element array, searching for 72 takes 4 comparisons while log₂(9) ≈ 3.17.

findings.summary: "First Occurrence (Lower Bound)" equates two routines that differ on a miss, contradicting the handbook's own lower-bound definition on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 sidebox: "1. First Occurrence (Lower Bound)" / "Goal: ==first index== of target, else -1"; page 3 sidebox: "4. Lower Bound" / "If all elements < target, return **n**".
findings.fix: Retitle to "First Occurrence (= lower bound when the target is present)" and add a line noting that lower bound returns the insertion point n while first occurrence returns -1.

findings.summary: The mistakes list flatly labels `while (low < high)` an error, though four templates in this set use it correctly.
findings.evidence: Cross-list item: "Loop condition `while (low < high)`" — yet page 1's upper-bound block notes "gotcha: loop is while (low < high)", and the upper-bound, pivot and peak templates on pages 3-5 all rely on it.
findings.fix: Qualify the item as "`while (low < high)` with `high = n - 1` in the classic search — it skips the last element; use `low <= high` there, and `low < high` only in the half-open bound/pivot/peak templates."

findings.summary: Page 2 opens with infinite-array range-doubling code, a topic its title does not cover and which the titles advertise for page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 2 title: "Loop Conditions, Dry Run & First/Last Occurrence"; its first block is `int low = 0, high = 1; while (arr[high] < target) { low = high; high = high * 2; }` with note "range doubles, so O(log n) expansions".
findings.fix: Move that code block to page 6 next to the infinite-array paragraph ("Example arr = [1,3,5,7,...], target = 14"), so page 2 starts with the loop-condition bullets its title promises.

findings.summary: Page 3 carries two differently-scoped items both numbered 5, so the numbering stops signalling where a section starts.
findings.evidence: Page 3 contains sidebox title "5. Upper Bound" (section 3) and, after the "4. Binary Search on Answer" heading, sidebox title "5. Monotonic Condition" (section 4).
findings.fix: Renumber the section-4 sideboxes from 1 within their own section (Monotonic Condition becomes "2. Monotonic Condition", matching "1. What is it?") so numbering restarts at each top-level heading.

findings.summary: The 2D matrix search snippet has no return after the loop, so the not-found path is missing.
findings.evidence: Code ends "  else high = mid - 1;","}" with note "n = number of columns; target 16 -> true" — no `return false;`, unlike the rotated-array snippet on page 5 whose note says "return false after loop".
findings.fix: Add `return false;` as the last line, or add "return false after loop" to the note.

findings.summary: The complexity table uses the symbol T in a bound without ever defining it.
findings.evidence: Page 6 table row `["BS on answer","O(log n * T)","O(1)"]`; T appears nowhere else in the content.
findings.fix: Change the cell to "O(log n * T), T = cost of isPossible" or add that gloss to the table caption.

findings.summary: Page 6's title names three smaller topics but omits Search Insert Position, which occupies the largest share of the page.
findings.evidence: Title: "Mountain, Infinite Arrays & 2D Matrix Search" — but the page devotes four consecutive blocks to insert position: bullets "Else return the index where it should be **inserted**", the table headed "Target (nums = [1,3,5,6])", and the callout "Insert pos = lower bound". Mountain is one code block and infinite arrays one paragraph.
findings.fix: Retitle page 6 to "Infinite Arrays, 2D Matrix & Search Insert Position" (drop "Mountain", which is a single spillover code block from page 5).
